newsitem.title: USA: Cycomm sees '97 profitability despite charge.
newsitem.headline: Cycomm sees '97 profitability despite charge.

text.p: Cycomm International Inc said Monday that it will take a non-recurring charge of about $159,000 this year, but also expects to be profitable for the first time in its history.
The company said it expects the charge to come mostly in the first quarter. It added that it sees revenues exceeding $20 million, with a significant backlog of orders.
The charge stems from a Securities and Exchange Commission ruling on the accounting treatment of convertible debentures the company issued last year.
"We found out about this last week," said Mike Scoff, Cycomm's chief financial officer, in a telephone interview.

The company said the accounting treatment required by the SEC resulted in non-recurring, non-cash charges of about $1.7 million and $1.2 million for the year ended May 31, 1996 and the seven months ended December 31, 1996, respectively, and will result in the 1997 charges.
Effective December 31, 1996, Cycomm changed its fiscal year end from May 31 to December 31.
Convertible debentures totalling $12,325,000 were privately placed to finance the company's working capital and acquisitions of XL Computing and XL Canada.
The company said the convertible debentures require it to issue stock at a discount to the debenture holders calculated at the time of conversion.
